_comment: Per-edit mutation engine config (spec: docs/design/per-edit-cloud-mutation-testing.md). Auto-loaded by bare `npx stryker run` — including inside the cloud mutation Worker's Sandbox, whose runner does `stryker run --mutate <file>`. ignorePatterns MUST exclude .interlinked/: Stryker sandboxes by copying the tree and crashes on the harness's Unix socket (found live 2026-07-02). The vitest configFile keeps the per-mutant suite scoped so runs stay in seconds.
_mutate_comment: Default target only. Every real run overrides it: the cloud runner does `stryker run --mutate <file>` for the edited file, and the detector-recall sweep (verification-density program Phase 3) points it at a detector. Left narrow so a bare `npx stryker run` is fast rather than a whole-repo job.
_mutator_comment: Operator coverage is DECLARED, not inherited. Stryker's defaults are a moving target across versions, and a silently-shrinking operator set weakens every mutation score in the repo without changing a single number in a baseline — exactly the drift the baseline-integrity gate exists to stop elsewhere. excludedMutations is empty on purpose: the full operator set is in force, and `stryker-mutators.test.ts` pins that.
_ignore_comment: Stryker sandboxes by COPYING the tree, once per run. Anything large and irrelevant here is paid for on every single file measured. `coverage` and `scratch` were added 2026-08-05 after a 2-test scope died with 'FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit' — coverage/ alone was 54MB across 1111 files (lcov-report is an HTML file per source file), and scratch/ held 22MB of prior mutation output. Neither is input to any test. `.interlinked` MUST stay listed: the tree-copy crashes outright on the harness's Unix socket (found live 2026-07-02).
_ignore_comment3: Every entry is ROOT-ANCHORED with a leading slash. Stryker's ignorePatterns are gitignore-style, so an unanchored `docs` matches ANY nested directory of that name — including test fixtures. Measured 2026-08-05: the structure-extractor tests failed the dry run with `expected [] to include 'docs/README.md'` because their fixture repo's own docs/ folder was stripped out of the sandbox. Unanchored entries silently delete fixture data, which surfaces as a test failure with no hint of the real cause.
_ignore_comment4: `/.stryker-tmp` must be listed EXPLICITLY. Stryker auto-ignores the temp dir only under its DEFAULT name, and this repo sets a per-run `tempDirName` of `.stryker-tmp/<runId>` for isolation — so each run ignored its own sandbox but happily copied its SIBLINGS'. With two shards that is a race: one run walks the other's sandbox while the other finishes and deletes it, and the copy dies with `ENOENT: scandir .stryker-tmp/<otherRun>/sandbox-XXXX/...`. Measured 2026-08-05: 15 of 48 files (31%) failed this way before the parent was ignored.
_ignore_comment5: `/docs/*` + `!/docs/generated` (2026-08-10, same class of bug as _ignore_comment2's skills/scripts incident): docs-freshness.test.ts asserts existsSync(docs/generated) and is graph-reachable from any file rules-loader.ts pulls DEFAULT_CONFIG/getBuiltinRules from (e.g. default-config.ts, builtin-rules-security.ts) — a whole-`/docs` exclusion silently pruned that directory from the sandbox, so the Stryker dry run failed with 'generated docs directory exists / expected false to be true' and the file became unmeasurable. `/docs/*` still excludes every OTHER top-level docs entry (design 2.8M, plans, external-pulse, marketing, the loose .md files) and its recursion never happens for them (directory-level exclusion prunes the whole subtree, same cost as before); the negation only re-admits the 100K `generated/` leaf a real test reads. Traced against project-reader.js's actual Minimatch+flipNegate directory-pruning logic before landing this, not guessed.
_ignore_comment2: `skills` (228K) and `scripts` (240K) were REMOVED from this list 2026-08-05: excluding them broke the dry run for any scope containing a test that reads them — `findEnforceSkillSource returns a non-null path` failed with 'expected null not to be null' purely because skills/ was absent from the sandbox. The sandbox must contain everything the selected tests read; the saving was a few hundred KB against a whole file becoming unmeasurable. `docs` stays excluded EXCEPT `docs/generated` (see _ignore_comment5) — the rest of docs (4.9M) still has no test reading it.
